spec.name: Earnings drift v9
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits: The strategy was tested with only 5 trials, which is insufficient to establish statistical robustness for a signal-based strategy. The performance metrics, while modest, lack a rigorous out-of-sample validation process.

verdict.opinion: The strategy relies on a simple earnings surprise signal. While the performance metrics are not suspiciously high, the research log indicates a very small number of trials (5) and distinct specifications (2). This suggests the strategy has not been sufficiently stress-tested against different market regimes or parameter variations. Given the lack of out-of-sample testing or rigorous validation, deploying real capital is premature. I recommend paper trading to verify that the signal captures real-world alpha and that the 10 bps cost assumption holds under actual execution conditions.
